syllabus_topics: Introduction: historical perspective of the importance of human-machine interaction in computer engineering and computer science.
Paradigm examples of interactive technologies, devices, systems, services, and applications.
The iterative and incremental development process of interactive systems and services.
Idea generation and evaluation: methods and techniques for prototyping: low, medium, and high fidelity.
Methods and techniques for analyzing users and usage contexts.
Predictive evaluation, heuristic evaluation, and participatory evaluation.
Design and construction of visual interfaces: interaction devices, styles, and technologies.
assessment_rules: The final grade for the normal period is calculated as 0.8 * Average(Nbake-off1, Nbake-off2) + 0.2 * Max(Average(Nmini-teste1, Nmini-teste2), Exam). A minimum grade of 9.5v is required on the final average of the laboratory assessment. The mini-test grade can be recovered in the normal exam period (the best grade between the mini-test average and the exam grade is counted). For student-workers, the two laboratory projects (bake-offs) have equal weight and account for 100% of the final grade, performed individually. Student-workers may optionally participate in mini-tests, in which case the normal period calculation applies. Assessment in the special period consists of one project (100%).
bibliography: Manuel J. Fonseca, Pedro Campos, Daniel Gonçalves, Introdução ao Design de Interfaces (3ª Edição), FCA, 2017 (Out.)
Alan Dix et al., Human-Computer Interaction (3rd ed.), Prentice Hall, 2004
Jenny Preece et al., Interaction Design – beyond computer interaction (3rd ed.), John Wiley, 2011
institution: Universidade De Lisboa — LERC Eng. de Telecomunicações e Informática (IST)
degree: Licenciatura em Engenharia de Telecomunicações e Informática (LERC)
